analysis.title: GS Codacci-Pisanelli - Macro Roadmap 2 Oct 2026
key_insights: Europe has been the epicentre of global rate volatility over the last month. A sharp curve flattening spread into France and a broader sovereign spread widening. The initial catalyst for this week's front-end-led widening was deleveraging.
Broader spread widening and bear flattening of credit curves shifted momentum for European duration locally, with bunds catching a flight-to-quality bid.

European FCI tightening is modest, 35bp over the last month and 15bp ytd, equal to about 0.15pp off year-ahead growth. This ratifies the ECB's cautious pace of hikes. Sequential hikes are much less likely and October ECB pricing is down to 4bp.

TPI support for sovereign spreads looks unlikely for now because spread levels are some way off worrying levels. France's eligibility without further fiscal commitment is also in question, so further widening is probably needed to force action.

The author sees a US-centric AI capex cycle pushing the cost of capital higher globally. This is sustainable in the US given high nominal growth, but Europe, with growth of about 1%, may pay the funding cost without enough of the benefit. Structural cross-market divergence trades in the European belly versus the US may be the longer-term trade.

30y real yields are about 70bp higher year-to-date and above 3%, a steady drift that has accelerated in recent weeks. Demand has not appeared in size and public and private supply is not slowing. Buybacks, SLR relief, WAM shortening and QT design changes have had only micro impacts in ASW and curve.

Long-end rates moved nearly 2sd higher in recent weeks while equities remain close to their highs. Rates pricing has swung from a cutting cycle to a material hiking cycle, yet FCIs are only 40bp tighter on the year, half of it in the last two weeks.

Reversal catalysts for rates are a slowdown in AI capex (power/regulatory bottlenecks or ROI doubts), fiscal tightening (a long way off), or a cyclical shift or inflation relief, with Europe the clearest pathway. Fresh shorts in rates are hard to advocate after the move. Rallies in rates likely stay shallow absent a change in the AI outlook or further macro deterioration.

Williams and Jefferson leaned dovish and core PCE was softer, pushing October FOMC pricing lower. GIR now looks for 3.0% core PCE on a Q4/Q4 basis, versus 3.4% for the median FOMC participant. NFP job growth was slightly weaker than expected with downward revisions, and wage growth was softer.

Long-end stress is driven by real rates, not breakevens. A hawkish Fed can help stop breakevens adding to the move but does little for the real rate trend. GS expects Fed hikes to exacerbate a K-shaped economy, with housing and lower income quartiles diverging from the AI boom.
If the macro calms into year end, the pathway exists for an equity rip higher, supported by the strength of the AI micro story.

trade_ideas.rationale: Europe may not sustain these rate and funding levels with growth around 1%, while the US has high enough nominal growth to do so.

risk_factors: European fragmentation risk and sovereign spread widening, especially France with its deficit path and upcoming election.
Continued rise in global cost of capital from the AI capex cycle.
Supply/demand imbalance in long-end duration with public and private supply not slowing.
Fed reaction function is hard to predict, and hikes may deepen a K-shaped US economy.
A slowdown in AI capex from power/regulatory bottlenecks or ROI doubts.

tension_points.bull_case: The widening is a severe bout of deleveraging, with modest FCI tightening so far and the ECB likely to keep its cautious quarterly pace.
tension_points.bear_case: It is the first sign of cracks from a structurally higher global cost of capital that Europe, with growth near 1%, cannot sustain, especially France.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further spread widening that forces the ECB to use TPI and forces France to commit to fiscal action.

tension_points.bull_case: Equities remain near highs on AI strength, and a calmer macro sets up a rip higher into year end.
tension_points.bear_case: A near-2sd long-end rate sell-off and rising real yields could eventually break something, with Europe the clearest pathway.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A slowdown in AI capex through power or regulatory bottlenecks or doubts about ROI.
